writeup.headline: Tenable rates Buy on strong price trend, solid balance sheet and raised guidance, but sits near Hold.
writeup.thesis: Tenable scores 67, a Buy, only 3 points above the Hold line. The strongest drivers are the trend score of 93, with the price at its 52-week high and shares 117.8 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days, and a balance sheet score of 86 with net debt at 0.21x free cash flow. Quality scores 67: a 78.0% gross margin and 25.3% FCF margin with the diluted share count down 6.0% year on year, offset by a thin 3.6% operating margin and stock-based pay at 17.2% of revenue. Growth (51) is modest, with TTM revenue growth of 9.9% and growth slowed by 1.0 pp from the previous quarter. Valuation (51) is mixed: in absolute terms P/FCF of 20.3x is moderate while EV/EBIT of 146.0x is high; against its own history P/S is cheaper than at 41 of the last 61 month-ends and P/FCF is cheaper than at 42 of the last 61 month-ends, while EV/EBIT is not comparable (negative in 55 of 61 month-ends), and news risk (71) is helped by a beat-and-raise quarter.
key_risks: Revenue growth is slowing, with latest-quarter revenue growth of 8.6% year on year.
GAAP profitability is thin: a 3.6% operating margin and EV/EBIT of 146.0x, high in absolute terms.
Stock-based compensation equals 17.2% of revenue, flattering free cash flow.
After a sharp run, the price is 71.1% above its 200-day average, leaving room for a pullback.
Analyst consensus remains Hold despite recent price target increases.
what_would_change: A drop of 3 points in the score, such as a fading trend score after the rally, would move the rating to Hold.
Further growth deceleration or a weaker news picture could push the score below 65.
Reaching Strong Buy needs 13 more points, likely requiring re-accelerating revenue growth and better operating margins.
A lower valuation in absolute terms, such as FCF yield moving above the 10-year Treasury yield, would lift the valuation score.
